The text sets it alongside the shaking of kingdoms, the destruction of Canaan's strongholds, and the ruin of the land of the Chaldeans by the Assyrians.

l: earth (the world), The Book of Isaiah
s: The earth is polluted by its inhabitants, who broke the everlasting covenant, and is devoured by a curse. Its foundations tremble as it is shaken and staggers like a drunkard. Decreed by the LORD, it will be emptied and laid waste, falling under its disobedience, never to rise.

l: inhabitants of the earth, The Book of Isaiah
s: The inhabitants of the earth broke the everlasting covenant, transgressed laws and violated statutes, and are found guilty under a curse. Judgment strikes every class, leaving few after burning; fear, pit and snare prevent escape, joy ends and cities desolate, while a remnant shouts the LORD's majesty.

l: everlasting covenant (with David), The Book of Isaiah
s: The LORD promises to make an everlasting covenant with the listeners, described as the sure mercies of David. In connection with it, he says he has given a witness, a leader and commander, to the peoples, and that nations will run to the one he has glorified.

l: day of judgment, The Book of Isaiah
s: "That day" is a coming judgment when the LORD punishes the army of the high ones and the kings of the earth. They are gathered like prisoners in a pit, shut up in prison, and visited after many days. The moon and sun are shamed as the LORD of Armies reigns in Zion.

l: the fortified city (city made a heap), The Book of Isaiah
s: A fortified city the LORD turned into a heap and ruin, now a palace of strangers no longer a city, declared never to be rebuilt.

l: all peoples, The Book of Isaiah
s: has covering and veil [to be destroyed] All peoples will be given a feast of choice meat and well refined choice wines by the LORD of Armies on this mountain. The covering that covers them and the veil spread over all nations will be destroyed.

l: feast, The Book of Isaiah
s: consists_of choice meat and wines [full of marrow, well refined] The LORD of Armies will make a feast for all peoples in this mountain, of choice meat full of marrow and well refined choice wines.

l: death, The Book of Isaiah
s: has_state swallowed up [forever] Death is said to be swallowed up forever by the Lord GOD. Along with this, tears are wiped from all faces.

l: strong city (Judah's), The Book of Isaiah
s: A strong city in Judah, celebrated in its song, whose walls and bulwarks are salvation appointed by God; its gates open for the faithful righteous nation.

l: righteous nation, The Book of Isaiah
s: keeps faith The righteous nation is the one that keeps faith and is invited to enter through the opened gates. The way of the just is uprightness, and the path of the righteous is made level.

l: lofty city, The Book of Isaiah
s: is_brought_down_by LORD [laid low to the dust] The lofty city is where those who dwell on high live, and the LORD brings it down, laying it low to the ground and to the dust. The feet of the poor and the steps of the needy tread it down.

l: wicked, The Book of Isaiah
s: The wicked are those who fail to learn righteousness even when shown favor, act wrongfully in uprightness's land, and miss the LORD's majesty and lifted hand; finally they see his zeal and are disappointed as fire consumes adversaries.

l: speakers (the people of Judah), The Book of Isaiah
s: The people of Judah, speaking together, long for the LORD and his name, seeking him by night. They admit other lords ruled them yet pledge to acknowledge only him, liken their trouble to labor that birthed wind, and are told to hide until indignation passes.

l: the dead, The Book of Isaiah
s: has_state not live [the departed spirits of the enemies' dead; destroyed by the LORD] The dead of the oppressors are said not to live; their departed spirits shall not rise, and the LORD has destroyed them and caused all memory of them to perish. By contrast, the LORD's dead shall live and their bodies arise, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits. The earth will also disclose her blood and no longer cover her slain.

l: resurrection, The Book of Isaiah
s: applies_to the dead [the LORD's dead shall live and arise] The text declares that the LORD's dead shall live and their dead bodies shall arise. Those who dwell in the dust are told to awake and sing, for the LORD's dew is like the dew of herbs and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.

l: leviathan, The Book of Isaiah
s: is_a serpent [fleeing and twisted; also called the dragon in the sea] Leviathan is described as the fleeing serpent and the twisted serpent. The LORD will punish it with his sword on that day, and he will also kill the dragon that is in the sea.

l: vineyard (the LORD's vineyard), The Book of Isaiah
s: has_quality pleasant The vineyard is called "a pleasant vineyard," and people are told to sing to it on that day. The LORD says he keeps it, waters it every moment, and guards it night and day so that no one damages it. He would battle and burn any briers and thorns found in it, unless they take hold of his strength and make peace.

l: those ready to perish and outcasts, The Book of Isaiah
s: Those ready to perish in Assyria and outcasts in Egypt are gathered back when a great trumpet sounds, then come to worship the LORD in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

l: the day of the LORD's judgment and restoration, The Book of Isaiah
s: "That day" is the LORD's day of judgment and restoration: he punishes leviathan and kills the dragon, the vineyard is sung about, he threshes from the Euphrates to Egypt's brook, gathers Israel one by one, and a great trumpet brings the perishing and outcasts to worship at Jerusalem.

l: forgiveness of Jacob's iniquity, The Book of Isaiah
s: has_fruit altar stones made like chalk stones [Asherah poles and incense altars rise no more] The text says Jacob's iniquity will be forgiven by this means, and that this is all the fruit of taking away his sin. The sign is that the LORD makes all the stones of the altar like chalk stones beaten in pieces, so that the Asherah poles and incense altars rise no more.

l: priest and prophet, The Book of Isaiah
s: A priest and prophet habitually reel from wine and strong drink, swallowed up by it; consequently they err in vision, stumble in judgment, and their tables fill with filthy vomit.

l: scoffers who rule in Jerusalem, The Book of Isaiah
s: Scoffers ruling in Jerusalem claim a covenant with death and agreement with Sheol, taking refuge in lies. They are told to hear the LORD, who says hail and waters will sweep away their refuge, annul their covenant, and warns against scoffing lest their bonds tighten.

l: cornerstone (laid in Zion), The Book of Isaiah
s: A precious, tried cornerstone of sure foundation, laid in Zion by the Lord GOD; believers will not act hastily, and justice and righteousness become the measuring and plumb lines.

l: covenant with death, The Book of Isaiah
s: has_fate annulled The covenant with death, along with the agreement with Sheol, is the claim by which the rulers believe the scourge will not reach them. The Lord declares it will be annulled and will not stand.

l: overflowing scourge, The Book of Isaiah
s: passes_through morning by morning, day and night [recurring; seizes those it passes] The overflowing scourge is what the scoffers believe will not come to them. The Lord says it will pass through and trample them, seizing them morning by morning, by day and by night, bringing nothing but terror to understand the message.

l: farming analogy, The Book of Isaiah
s: A farming analogy in Chapter 28: a farmer does not plow endlessly but levels soil and plants dill, cumin, wheat, barley and spelt in place. Dill and cumin are beaten gently with stick and rod, and flour isn't ground endlessly. God teaches this right judgment, which comes from the LORD of Armies' counsel.

l: Ariel, The Book of Isaiah
s: Ariel is the city where David encamped. The LORD will distress, besiege, and humble it into an altar hearth amid mourning, its voice muttering from the dust; then the LORD of Armies will visit with thunder, earthquake, and fire, and its enemies vanish.

l: nations that fight against Ariel, The Book of Isaiah
s: A multitude of nations attacking Ariel, her stronghold, and Mount Zion; they will become like fine dust and chaff, vanishing instantly like a dream leaving a hungry dreamer unsatisfied.

l: prophets and seers, The Book of Isaiah
s: has_state spirit of deep sleep [poured out by the LORD; eyes closed] The prophets and seers have their eyes closed and heads covered by the LORD, who has poured on them a spirit of deep sleep. All vision has become to them like a sealed book that neither the educated nor the uneducated can read.

l: this people, The Book of Isaiah
s: A people who honor the LORD with their mouths and lips while their hearts stay distant, their fear of him merely a taught human commandment; the LORD will respond with a marvelous work, destroying their wise men's wisdom and hiding prudence.

l: rebellious children (Judah's people), The Book of Isaiah
s: A rebellious people, Judah's lying children, make an alliance with Egypt without consulting the LORD, send riches there, trust in horses and flight, and refuse the offered rest. They are warned they will flee, left like a beacon on a mountain, then promised grace, guidance, idol removal, provision, healing, and dwelling in Zion.

l: alliance with Egypt, The Book of Isaiah
s: The alliance is portrayed as a sin added to sin, made without the LORD's Spirit or advice, with envoys at Zoan and Hanes and riches carried through dangerous lands. The LORD says it will profit nothing and bring only shame and reproach.

l: those who help Egypt (reliance on Egypt), The Book of Isaiah
s: Those who go down to Egypt for help, trusting its many strong horses, chariots and horsemen instead of the Holy One of Israel, are met with woe; the LORD stretches out his hand, so helper and helped stumble, fall and are consumed together.

l: fool, The Book of Isaiah
s: The fool speaks folly, works iniquity in heart, utters error against the LORD, and deprives the hungry and thirsty; in the coming reign he will no longer be called noble.

l: scoundrel, The Book of Isaiah
s: A scoundrel with evil ways devises wicked plans, using lying words to destroy the humble even when the needy speak rightly; he will no longer be highly respected.

l: noble, The Book of Isaiah
s: devises noble things [continues in them] The noble devises noble things and will continue in noble things. This stands in contrast to the fool and the scoundrel.

l: women at ease, The Book of Isaiah
s: Careless, at-ease women, called careless daughters, are commanded to rise, hear, tremble, strip, wear sackcloth, and mourn pleasant fields and vines, because vintage and harvest will fail after days beyond a year.

l: my people, The Book of Isaiah
s: My people are a group whose land will be overgrown with thorns and briers after desolation, yet they will afterward dwell in peaceful habitation, safe dwellings, and quiet resting places, despite hail and a leveled city.

l: joyous city, The Book of Isaiah
s: The joyous city, once full of houses of joy and a populous palace, is foretold to be overgrown with thorns and briers, forsaken and deserted, its hill and watchtower becoming permanent dens for wild donkeys and flocks.

l: Spirit, The Book of Isaiah
s: is_poured_on my people [from on high, future] The desolation will last until the Spirit is poured on us from on high. This outpouring marks the turning point at which the wilderness becomes a fruitful field.

l: wilderness, The Book of Isaiah
s: A wilderness that, once the Spirit is poured out, becomes a fruitful field, and justice then dwells in it.

l: fruitful field, The Book of Isaiah
s: A fruitful field, after the Spirit is poured out, is reckoned a forest while the wilderness becomes fruitful, and righteousness remains there.

l: righteousness, The Book of Isaiah
s: Righteousness is the foundation of the king's reign, remaining in the fruitful field; its work is peace, and its effect lasting quietness and confidence forever.

l: vintage and harvest failure, The Book of Isaiah
s: affects women at ease [troubles them] The vintage will fail and the harvest won't come, which troubles the careless women. The people are to mourn the pleasant fields and the fruitful vine.

l: destroyer (the one who destroys and betrays), The Book of Isaiah
s: faces destruction and betrayal [after finishing destroying and betraying] The destroyer is met with a woe because he destroys and betrays though he himself was not destroyed or betrayed. When he finishes, he will be destroyed and betrayed in turn. He is also described as breaking the covenant and despising cities and man, and his rigging is later shown untied while the lame divide his plunder.

l: sinners in Zion, The Book of Isaiah
s: feel fear [trembling seizes the godless] The sinners in Zion are afraid and trembling seizes the godless among them. They ask who can live with the devouring fire and everlasting burning.

l: righteous man, The Book of Isaiah
s: The righteous man is a figure of integrity who walks righteously, speaks blamelessly, rejects bribes and oppressive gain, and avoids evil. He is rewarded with a secure high fortress, steady bread and water, and the sight of the king and a distant land.

l: nations, The Book of Isaiah
s: has_armies_subject_to slaughter The nations and peoples are summoned to hear, along with the earth and all it contains. The LORD is enraged against them and their armies, has utterly destroyed them, and has given them over to slaughter. Their slain are cast out, a stench rises from their bodies, and the mountains melt in their blood.

l: sword (the LORD's sword), The Book of Isaiah
s: The LORD's sword has drunk its fill in the sky and then comes down on Edom for judgment. It is filled with blood and covered with fat, the blood of lambs and goats and the fat of the kidneys of rams.

l: sacrifice (the LORD's sacrifice in Bozrah), The Book of Isaiah
s: The LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, accompanied by a great slaughter in the land of Edom. The sacrifice is pictured with the blood and fat of lambs, goats and rams on the LORD's sword, and wild oxen and bulls come down with them so that the land is drunk with blood and its dust made greasy with fat.

l: year of the LORD's favor and day of vengeance, The Book of Isaiah
s: The LORD has a day of vengeance, described also as a year of recompense for the cause of Zion. Its results are seen in the burning pitch and sulfur of Edom's land, which is never quenched and stays desolate forever.

l: desolate-land creatures (Edom's inhabitants), The Book of Isaiah
s: The pelican, porcupine, owl and raven possess and dwell in Edom, joined by jackals, ostriches, wolves, the wild goat, the night creature, the arrow snake and kites. Each has its mate, and none is missing, because the LORD's mouth commanded it and his Spirit gathered them. He cast the lot and divided the land to them with a measuring line, so they will possess it forever, from generation to generation.

l: wilderness (the desert land), The Book of Isaiah
s: The wilderness is a dry desert land that is promised transformation: it will rejoice and blossom like a rose, receive the glory of Lebanon, Carmel and Sharon, and gain waters, streams, pools and springs, with grass, reeds and rushes where jackals lay.

l: The Holy Way, The Book of Isaiah
s: The Holy Way is a highway in the wilderness, set apart for those who walk in the Way. The redeemed walk there, while unclean and wicked fools cannot pass and no lion or ravenous animal will be found on it.

l: The Holy People, The LORD’s Redeemed, The Book of Isaiah
s: The Holy People are the LORD's ransomed, redeemed ones. Across both chapters, they belong to the LORD and are recalled as those for whom he made the sea's depths a path. They walk the Holy Way and return to Zion singing, crowned with everlasting joy and gladness, while sorrow and sighing flee.

l: blind, deaf, lame and mute (the afflicted healed), The Book of Isaiah
s: When God comes to save, the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped. The lame man will leap like a deer and the tongue of the mute will sing.

l: waters and streams (in the wilderness), The Book of Isaiah
s: A promised transformation of the wilderness by the LORD: rivers open on bare heights, springs fill valleys, and desert and dry land become pools and springs, answering the poor and needy seeking water. He plants cedar, acacia, myrtle, oil, cypress, pine and box, so all see his hand created it.

l: joy and gladness (everlasting joy replacing sorrow), The Book of Isaiah
s: replaces sorrow and sighing [sorrow and sighing flee away] The wilderness will rejoice with joy and singing, and the ransomed will have everlasting joy on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, while sorrow and sighing flee away.

l: Sennacherib, The Book of Isaiah
s: Sennacherib is the king of Assyria. He captures Judah's fortified cities and sends Rabshakeh with an army from Lachish to Jerusalem. While warring against Libnah, he writes to Hezekiah that Jerusalem's God cannot save it. The LORD denounces his pride and turns him back; his army is struck and he returns to Nineveh, where his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer kill him and Esar Haddon reigns.

l: Rabshakeh, The Book of Isaiah
s: Rabshakeh is the Assyrian king's envoy, sent from Lachish to Jerusalem with a large army. By the aqueduct he mocks Judah's trust in Egypt and the LORD, refuses Aramaic, and calls out in the Jews' language, offering peace and a good land for surrender while denying any god can deliver from Assyria. Hezekiah's messengers later say his words defy the living God; he returns to find the king fighting at Libnah.
